translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Yang Chun was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，姚仲攻德順軍，敗金人於瓦亭砦、新店。

translations.literal: Day renchen: Yao Zhong attacked Deshun army and defeated the Jin at Wating fort and Xindian.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Yao Zhong attacked Deshun and beat the Jin at Wating fort and Xindian.

sentences.zh: 是月，張安國等攻殺耿京，李寶將王世隆攻破安國，執之以獻。

translations.literal: That month Zhang Anguo and others attacked and killed Geng Jing; Li Bao's officer Wang Shilong broke Anguo and presented him captive.
translations.idiomatic: That month Zhang Anguo and others killed Geng Jing; Li Bao's Wang Shilong broke Anguo and sent him in bonds.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丁卯朔，姚仲遣兵救原州。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day dingmao new moon: Yao Zhong sent troops to relieve Yuan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, dingmao new moon: Yao Zhong sent troops to relieve Yuan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 己巳，使侍從、台諫條上防秋足食足民策。

translations.literal: Day jisi: attendant and remonstrance officials were told to submit policies for autumn defense with full grain and settled people.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, attendants and remonstrators were told to submit autumn-defense plans with full stores and settled people.

sentences.zh: 遣左武大夫都飛虎結約河東。

translations.literal: Left Martial Grandee Du Feihu was sent to treat with allies in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Left Martial Grandee Du Feihu was sent to ally with Hedong.

sentences.zh: 壬申，賞禦營宿衛將士四萬餘人進官有差。

translations.literal: Day renshen: more than forty thousand Imperial Guard soldiers were advanced in rank by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, over forty thousand Imperial Guard soldiers were promoted by degrees.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，蠲淮東殘破州軍上供銀絹、米麥及經、總製錢一年。

translations.literal: Day guiyou: tribute silver, silk, grain, and consolidated funds from ravaged Huai east prefectures and armies were remitted for one year.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, tribute silver, silk, grain, and consolidated funds from ravaged Huai east districts were forgiven one year.

sentences.zh: 蒙城縣民倪震率丁口數千來歸。

translations.literal: Mengcheng commoner Ni Zhen led several thousand households to come over.
translations.idiomatic: Mengcheng commoner Ni Zhen led several thousand households to defect.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，募民耕淮東荒田，蠲其徭役及租稅七年。

translations.literal: Day jiaxu: commoners were recruited to farm wasteland in Huai east; corvée and rent were remitted seven years.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, commoners were recruited to farm Huai-east wasteland with seven years' corvée and rent forgiven.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以御史中丞汪澈參知政事。

translations.literal: Day wuyin: Censor-in-Chief Wang Che was made Participation Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Censor-in-Chief Wang Che became Participation Councillor.

sentences.zh: 金人圍海州。

translations.literal: The Jin besieged Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin besieged Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 戊子，洪邁等辭行，報聘書用敵國禮。

translations.literal: Day wuzi: Hong Mai and others declined to go; the return mission used enemy-state ritual.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Hong Mai and others declined the mission; the reply used enemy-state ritual.

sentences.zh: 是月，大雨，淮水暴溢數百里，漂沒廬舍，人畜死者甚眾。

translations.literal: That month great rain made the Huai overflow for hundreds of li, sweeping away houses; men and beasts died in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: That month heavy rain flooded the Huai for hundreds of li, washing away houses; countless people and animals drowned.

sentences.zh: 五月戊戌，吳璘自河池如鳳翔巡邊，姚仲遣兵救原州，數敗金人。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day wuxu: Wu Lin from Hechi went to Fengxiang to tour the border; Yao Zhong sent troops to relieve Yuan and several times defeated the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, wuxu: Wu Lin left Hechi for a Fengxiang border tour; Yao Zhong sent relief to Yuan and repeatedly beat the Jin.

sentences.zh: 庚子，復置提舉秦州買馬監，命四川總領官兼權其職。

translations.literal: Day gengzi: the Qinzhou horse-purchase intendant was restored; the Sichuan overall finance officer was also given acting charge.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, the Qinzhou horse-purchase intendant was restored under acting Sichuan overall finance charge.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，姚仲及金人戰于原州北嶺，敗績。

translations.literal: Day renyin: Yao Zhong fought the Jin on Yuan's north ridge and was beaten.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Yao Zhong fought the Jin on Yuan's north ridge and was routed.

sentences.zh: 戊申，復以楊存中為醴泉觀使，奉朝請。

translations.literal: Day wushen: Yang Cunzhong was again made commissioner of the Liquan Abbey and court attendee.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Yang Cunzhong was again made Liquan Abbey commissioner and court attendee.

sentences.zh: 罷禦營宿衛司。

translations.literal: The Imperial Guard office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Guard office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，鎮江都統制張子蓋救海州，遇金人于石湫堰，大敗之，金人解去。

translations.literal: Day xinhai: Zhenjiang overall commander Zhang Zigai relieved Haizhou, met the Jin at Shiquyan, routed them, and the Jin lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Zhenjiang commander Zhang Zigai relieved Haizhou, met the Jin at Shiquyan, routed them, and the siege lifted.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，命張浚專一措置兩淮事務兼節制淮東西、沿江州郡軍馬。

translations.literal: Day jiayin: Zhang Jun was given sole charge of the two Huai and concurrent control of Huai east and west and riverine prefecture armies.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Zhang Jun was given sole charge of the two Huai and control of Huai east and west and riverine armies.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，知順昌軍孟昭率部曲來歸。

translations.literal: Day yimao: Shunchang army commander Meng Zhao led his followers to come over.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Shunchang commander Meng Zhao and his men defected.

sentences.zh: 己未，吳璘遣將復熙州。

translations.literal: Day jiwei: Wu Lin sent generals to recover Xi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Wu Lin's generals retook Xi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，禁諸軍互招逃亡。

translations.literal: Day renxu: armies were forbidden to recruit one another's deserters.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, armies were forbidden to recruit one another's deserters.

sentences.zh: 加鄭藻太尉。

translations.literal: Zheng Zao was advanced to Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zao was made Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 振東北流民。

translations.literal: Northeast refugees were relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast refugees were relieved.

sentences.zh: 命張浚置御前萬弩營，募淮民為之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun was ordered to establish an Imperial Front Ten-Thousand Crossbow Camp recruiting Huai commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun was told to form an Imperial Front Ten-Thousand Crossbow Camp from Huai recruits.

sentences.zh: 甲子，詔立建王瑋為皇太子，更名昚。

translations.literal: Day jiazi: an edict established the Prince of Jian, Wei, as heir apparent; his name was changed to Shen.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, the Prince of Jian, Wei, was made heir apparent and renamed Shen.

sentences.zh: 加成閔太尉、主管殿前司，李顯忠為太尉、主管馬軍司。

translations.literal: Cheng Min was advanced to Grand Marshal and put in charge of the Palace Front Office; Li Xianzhong to Grand Marshal and in charge of the Palace Horse Office.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Min became Grand Marshal and headed the Palace Front Office; Li Xianzhong Grand Marshal and headed the Palace Horse Office.

sentences.zh: 籍諸州歸正人，願為農者給官田，復租十年；

translations.literal: Returnees in every prefecture were registered; those wishing to farm were given official fields with ten years' rent remitted;
translations.idiomatic: Returnees in every prefecture were registered; farmers received official fields with ten years' rent forgiven;

sentences.zh: 願為兵者赴軍中。

translations.literal: those wishing to be soldiers went to the armies.
translations.idiomatic: those wishing to soldier went to the armies.

sentences.zh: 六月丙寅朔，吳璘次大幽嶺，檄召姚仲至軍前，下河池獄，命夔路安撫使李師顏代將其兵。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day bingyin new moon: Wu Lin halted at Dayou ridge, summoned Yao Zhong to headquarters, imprisoned him at Hechi, and Kui-route pacification commissioner Li Shiyan replaced his command.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, bingyin new moon: Wu Lin stopped at Dayou ridge, summoned Yao Zhong, jailed him at Hechi, and Kui pacification commissioner Li Shiyan took his command.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，名新宮曰德壽。

translations.literal: Day wuchen: the new palace was named Deshou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, the new palace was named Deshou.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以吳珙主管步軍司。

translations.literal: Day gengwu: Wu Gong was put in charge of the Palace Foot Office.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Wu Gong was put in charge of the Palace Foot Office.

sentences.zh: 罷三招討司。

translations.literal: The three reconquest offices were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The three reconquest offices were abolished.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，加贈兄子為太師、中書令，追封秀王，諡安僖；

translations.literal: Day jiaxu: the Emperor's nephew was posthumously advanced to Grand Preceptor and Secretariat Director, enfeoffed as Prince of Xiu with posthumous title Anxi;
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, the emperor's nephew was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Secretariat Director, enfeoffed Prince of Xiu as Anxi;

sentences.zh: 妻張氏封王夫人。

translations.literal: his wife Lady Zhang was enfeoffed Lady of the Princely House.
translations.idiomatic: his wife Lady Zhang was enfeoffed Lady of the Princely House.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，朱倬罷。

translations.literal: Day yihai: Zhu Zhuo was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Zhu Zhuo was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 丙子，詔皇太子即皇帝位。

translations.literal: Day bingzi: an edict ordered the heir apparent to take the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, the heir apparent was ordered to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝稱太上皇帝，退處德壽宮，皇后稱太上皇后。

translations.literal: The Emperor styled himself Retired Emperor, withdrew to Deshou Palace, and the Empress styled herself Retired Empress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the title Retired Emperor, withdrew to Deshou Palace, and the empress became Retired Empress.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，累上尊號曰光堯壽聖憲天體道性仁誠德經武緯文紹業興統明謨盛烈太上皇帝。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong took the throne, he repeatedly added honorifics until the full title Illustrious Yao, Long-lived, Sagely, Heaven-Aligned, All-Embracing, Innately Benevolent, Sincerely Virtuous, Classically Martial, Cosmically Literate, Continuing the Enterprise, Raising the Succession, Bright in Counsel, Grand in Achievement Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaozong's accession honorifics were piled on until the full title Illustrious Yao, Long-lived, Sagely, Heaven-Aligned, All-Embracing, Innately Benevolent, Sincerely Virtuous, Classically Martial, Cosmically Literate, Continuing the Enterprise, Raising the Succession, Bright in Counsel, Grand in Achievement Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十四年十月乙亥，崩于德壽殿，年八十一。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year of Chunxi, tenth month, day yihai: he died at Deshou Hall, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxi 14, tenth month, yihai: he died at Deshou Hall, aged eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 諡曰聖神武文憲孝皇帝，廟號高宗。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Sagely, Divine, Martial, Literate, Constitutional, Filial Emperor; temple name Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title Sagely, Divine, Martial, Literate, Constitutional, Filial Emperor; temple name Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 十六年三月丙寅，欑於會稽之永思陵。

translations.literal: Sixteenth year, third month, day bingyin: he was buried at Yongsi Mausoleum in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Year 16, third month, bingyin: he was buried at Yongsi Mausoleum in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 光宗紹熙二年，加諡受命中興全功至德聖神武文昭仁憲孝皇帝。

translations.literal: Second year of Shaoxi under Guangzong, the posthumous title was increased to Received the Mandate, Restored the Central Enterprise, Full Merit, Ultimate Virtue, Sagely, Divine, Martial, Literate, Illustrious, Benevolent, Constitutional, Filial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong's Shaoxi 2 added Received the Mandate, Restored the Central Enterprise, Full Merit, Ultimate Virtue, Sagely, Divine, Martial, Literate, Illustrious, Benevolent, Constitutional, Filial to the posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：昔夏後氏傳五世而後羿篡，少康復立而祀夏；

translations.literal: Appraisal: In antiquity the Xia passed five generations and then Hou Yi usurped; Shaokang restored the line and sacrificed to Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: In antiquity Xia passed five generations before Hou Yi usurped; Shaokang restored the line and sacrificed to Xia.

sentences.zh: 周傳九世而厲王死于彘，宣王復立而繼周；

translations.literal: Zhou passed nine generations and King Li died at Zhi; King Xuan restored the line and continued Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou passed nine generations before King Li died at Zhi; King Xuan restored Zhou.

sentences.zh: 漢傳十有一世而新莽竊位，光武復立而興漢；

translations.literal: Han passed eleven generations and Xin Mang seized the throne; Guangwu restored the line and revived Han.
translations.idiomatic: Han passed eleven generations before Xin Mang seized power; Guangwu restored Han.

sentences.zh: 晉傳四世有懷、湣之禍，元帝正位於建鄴；

translations.literal: Jin passed four generations and suffered the disasters of Emperors Huai and Min; Emperor Yuan took the throne at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin passed four generations to the disasters of Huai and Min; Emperor Yuan took the throne at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 唐傳六世有安、史之難，肅宗即位于靈武；

translations.literal: Tang passed six generations and suffered the An and Shi rebellion; Emperor Suzong took the throne at Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang passed six generations to the An–Shi rebellion; Emperor Suzong took the throne at Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 宋傳九世而徽、欽陷於金，高宗纘圖于南京：六君者，史皆稱為中興，而有異同焉。

translations.literal: Song passed nine generations and Huizong and Qinzong fell to the Jin; Gaozong continued the succession at the Southern Capital: these six rulers history all calls restorations, yet they differ.
translations.idiomatic: Song passed nine generations before Huizong and Qinzong fell to the Jin; Gaozong continued the line at the Southern Capital: history calls all six restorations, yet they differ.

sentences.zh: 夏經羿、浞，周曆共和，漢間新室、更始，晉、唐、宋則歲月相續者也。

translations.literal: Xia endured Yi and Zhuo; Zhou passed through the Gonghe regency; Han had the Xin and Gengshi interludes; Jin, Tang, and Song had unbroken succession by years.
translations.idiomatic: Xia endured Yi and Zhuo; Zhou had the Gonghe regency; Han the Xin and Gengshi interludes; Jin, Tang, and Song kept succession by the calendar.

sentences.zh: 蕭王、琅琊皆出疏屬，少康、宣王、肅宗、高宗則父子相承者也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiao and Langye both came from distant branches; Shaokang, King Xuan, Suzong, and Gaozong passed father to son.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiao and Langye came from distant branches; Shaokang, King Xuan, Suzong, and Gaozong succeeded father to son.

sentences.zh: 至於克復舊物，則晉元與宋高宗視四君者有餘責焉。

translations.literal: As for recovering the old realm, Jin's Yuan and Song's Gaozong fall short of the other four.
translations.idiomatic: In recovering the old realm, Jin's Yuan and Song's Gaozong fall short of the other four.

sentences.zh: 高宗恭儉仁厚，以之繼體守文則有餘，以之撥亂反正則非其才也。

translations.literal: Gaozong was respectful, frugal, benevolent, and generous — more than enough to inherit and preserve culture, but not the talent to set chaos right.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong was respectful, frugal, benevolent, and generous — fit to inherit and keep culture, but not to set chaos right.

sentences.zh: 況時危勢逼，兵弱財匱，而事之難處又有甚於數君者乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, danger pressed, armies were weak, funds exhausted, and the hardships he faced were worse than those other rulers' — were they not?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, danger pressed, armies were weak, funds exhausted, and his hardships exceeded those other rulers' — did they not?

sentences.zh: 君子于此，蓋亦有憫高宗之心，而重傷其所遭之不幸也。

translations.literal: The gentleman here surely pities Gaozong's heart and deeply mourns the misfortune he met.
translations.idiomatic: Here the gentleman surely pities Gaozong and mourns the misfortune he met.

sentences.zh: 然當其初立，因四方勤王之師，內相李綱，外任宗澤，天下之事宜無不可為者。

translations.literal: Yet when he first took the throne, with armies rallying from every quarter, Li Gang within and Zong Ze without, nothing under heaven should have been impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at his first enthronement, with armies rallying everywhere, Li Gang within and Zong Ze without, nothing should have been impossible.

sentences.zh: 顧乃播遷窮僻，重以苗、劉群盜之亂，權宜立國，確虖艱哉。

translations.literal: Instead he wandered to remote corners, again battered by the Miao and Liu bandit revolts — a state held by expediency, how hard it was!
translations.idiomatic: Instead he wandered to remote corners, battered again by Miao and Liu rebels — a state held by expediency, how hard!

sentences.zh: 其始惑于汪、黃，其終制於奸檜，恬墮猥懦，坐失事機。

translations.literal: At first he was misled by Wang Boyan and Huang Qianshan; in the end he was controlled by the traitor Qin, content to sink into cowardice and lose every chance.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was misled by Wang Boyan and Huang Qianshan; in the end controlled by traitor Qin, content in cowardice, losing every chance.

sentences.zh: 甚而趙鼎、張浚相繼竄斥，岳飛父子竟死于大功垂成之秋。

translations.literal: Worse still, Zhao Ding and Zhang Jun were driven out in turn, and Yue Fei father and son died just as great success was near.
translations.idiomatic: Worse, Zhao Ding and Zhang Jun were driven out in turn, and Yue Fei and his son died as success neared.

sentences.zh: 一時有志之士，為之扼腕切齒。

translations.literal: Men of purpose in that age clenched their fists and ground their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Men of purpose in that age clenched fists and ground teeth.

sentences.zh: 帝方偷安忍恥，匿怨忘親，卒不免于來世之誚，悲夫！

translations.literal: The Emperor instead sought ease and bore shame, hid resentment and forgot kin, and in the end could not escape blame from later ages — pitiful indeed!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instead sought ease and bore shame, hid resentment and forgot kin, and could not escape later ages' blame — pitiful indeed!
